relevance: Strong scalar foundation candidate for mixed binary32/binary64, integer conversion and quantized Linear arithmetic.
capability: Executable backend refinement equations for add/sub/mul/div/sqrt/FMA; source AffineQuantizer implements exact-rational nearest-even clamp(round(x/scale)+zeroPoint), dequantization and error theorems. Documentation includes mixed precision, reduction trees and certifying elementary functions.
limitations: Affine spec does not establish PT2E/XNNPACK dynamic per-channel kernel equivalence: runtime division/multiplication rounding, scale derivation, dtype promotion, clamp/tie order, accumulation and backend options need separate bridges. Wider deterministic transcendental approximations explicitly lack general error bounds; software spec/runtime correspondence still requires review.

relevance: Direct way to reason about Lean Float and Float32 after a Lean toolchain migration.
capability: Source transfers algebraic/order/conversion lemmas via RealFloat.ofFloat and ofFloat32; README describes binary64/binary32 equivalences and Lean4.33 model definitions.
limitations: Early library; proofs describe Lean logical Float.Model bodies, not an automatic PyTorch/XNNPACK/hardware contract. Toolchain version must be reconciled; no full transformer importer or quantization mapping found.

relevance: Strong explicit f32/f64 dot-product and reduction numerical-error building blocks.
capability: Source Native.Operations proves unpacked/word addition and multiplication refinement; documentation includes native Float/Float32 bridges, sequential/pairwise dot products, gradual-underflow bounds and executable range/accuracy certificates.
limitations: Evaluation order and range hypotheses matter; sequential unfused dot theorems do not certify XNNPACK reduction schedules or FMA use. Authors disclose primarily LLM-written formalization and incomplete independent standard-correspondence review.

relevance: Promising restricted Python/NumPy-to-Lean numerical verification workflow, especially f64 approximations and source contracts.
capability: Source native binary64 arithmetic bounds derive from Float.Model; Pipeline tracks finite native results versus an independent ideal real expression. Provider documentation covers bounded loops, selected arrays and optional Rust/Aeneas correspondence.
limitations: Restricted profiles only; BLAS calls, arbitrary Python and combining profiles need new semantic bridges. Runtime/frontend/source mapping remains trusted. No documented arbitrary PyTorch/PT2E transformer importer or XNNPACK per-channel quantization proof.

relevance: Exceptionally relevant model for proving packed quantization kernels preserve indexing and arithmetic inputs.
capability: DequantProof.lean proves int2/int4 bitvector decoding, per-axis/blocked write bijections, scale/zero-point indices, chunk bounds and disjoint output writes using kernel decide and arithmetic.
limitations: ONNX Runtime sub-byte DequantizeLinear, not our int8/PT2E dynamic Linear. C++ loop model manually transcribed; float expression is not modeled, size_t no-overflow assumed. Useful proof architecture rather than ready end-to-end compiler theorem.

relevance: Useful executable IEEE-style bitblasting library alongside SAT/bv_decide.
capability: Inspected packed/unpacked multiplication with exceptional cases and rounding modes; SMT-LIB semantics explicitly separates structural NaN equality from IEEE comparison. Directory now includes addition/division/FMA/sqrt beyond older README's multiplication focus.
limitations: Full semantic correctness and operation coverage must be audited individually; testing compatibility and a few algebraic theorems are not complete standard correspondence. Distinct from leanprover/fp-lean book. No PyTorch/XNNPACK frontend.

relevance: Flocq-style generic rounding/error and IEEE representations worth evaluating for mathematical specifications.
capability: Source PrimFloat constructs a proof-carrying StandardFloat binary64 model, validity witnesses and representation/operation equivalence theorems; documented VCFloat-style error layer.
limitations: README explicitly distinguishes no active sorry/project axioms from source-semantic fidelity and lists outstanding work. PrimFloat is a modeled Coq primitive binary64 layer, not evidence of an existing Lean native/PyTorch/host implementation bridge.

relevance: Mature-style conservative real enclosures for exp/log and approximation error proofs.
capability: Software Floating with directed bounds, Interval and Approx typeclasses; inspected hyperbolic source proves sinh/cosh enclosures compositionally from exp.
limitations: Conservative software interval results concern real functions; not bit-exact host tanh/exp or PyTorch inference. Need prove actual polynomial/kernel approximation and floating-point evaluation fit the interval contracts.

relevance: Relevant IR and memory proof architecture for translating ML kernels into Lean models.
capability: Python AST gather/tracing frontend; source semantics models tensor banks/chip memory, allocation and heap laws. FloatRep is parameterized; SymbolicFloat preserves exact operation order syntactically.
limitations: Initial target NKI/Trainium, not FPGA or PyTorch PT2E. Inspected FloatRep only requires Add and symbolic expressions; an IEEE instantiation and frontend/compiler correspondence must be established separately.

relevance: Useful dtype, slicing, byte serialization and executable tensor infrastructure.
capability: Inspected Float.lean implements float format/FP8 conversion helpers; MixedPrec.lean supplies error-bound scaffolding for FP8.
limitations: MixedPrec declares additional axioms including v=x+(v-x), cancellation and distributivity-like Float32 identities that are generally false for rounded IEEE arithmetic. Its numerical error theorems cannot be accepted as exact FP foundations without replacing these assumptions. Float source contains sorry warnings.

relevance: Potential typed AST/frontend component if source pipeline exports StableHLO.
capability: Parses generic StableHLO syntax to well-formed typed AST, reports unspecified/underspecified constructions; example JAX attention exporter.
limitations: Program analysis and typing do not establish numerical equivalence or supply a PT2E/XNNPACK importer.

relevance: Discovery pointer to ML kernel/tensor ecosystem.
capability: Meta-package linking SHerLOC, KLR and TensorLib.
limitations: No standalone end-to-end certification capability stated; assess components separately.

Lowering preservation inspected is kernelCount=opCount structural invariant, not numerical program equivalence; full semantic theorem is documented future work and witness obligations remain. README end-to-end claims must be read with these boundaries.

relevance: Highly relevant captured-PyTorch-to-Lean pattern for integer width specialization of generated kernels.
capability: Inspected NarrowGeneric.lean models i32/i64 promotion and wrapping, truncating division/remainder, masked loads and symbolic payloads; proves checker-accepted per-lane observable equality, definedness and argument packing with polynomial side conditions. limitations: Restricted 1D pointwise kernels, not arbitrary NN/PyTorch semantic import. Source extractor/exporter trusted with disclosed gaps; runtime guard installation assumed, original bounds/no aliasing assumed, TTIR→SASS/hardware trusted. relevance: Relevant whole-launch coverage and generated integer-index optimization case study.

relevance: Strong bitvector proof patterns for integer quantized Linear kernels and reference-loop correspondence.

limitations: Hand-transcribed model and PR tests tie source to compiled implementation. Float epilogue is not proved; assumes same IEEE operation sequence receives same integer. Weight bound≤15 and K≤2^15 ensure no signed-int32 overflow; not XNNPACK int8 dynamic per-channel implementation.

relevance: Useful mathematical basis for shape/stride view fusion and memory layout proofs.
capability: Inspected ViewMerging.lean states necessary/sufficient view merge criterion and supporting index composition lemmas.
limitations: Main proof dependencies and criterion contain sorry; offsets/masks absent. Positive Nat stride setting is narrower than general PyTorch views. No numerical/FP semantics.

relevance: One of the clearest discovered concrete machine-arithmetic-to-neural-specification bridges.
capability: SequentialBridge.lean proves modeled scalar PTX dense1024→3072+ReLU kernel returns and stores finite FP32 output within traceErrorBudget of actual upstream TorchLean Sequential real forward. RoundingError composes FloatLib half-ULP FMA and bias-add budgets; includes store frame property.
limitations: Hand-modeled PTX program/source correspondence; fixed architecture and sequential fused accumulation. Requires KernelEntry and finite result at each trace site, budget depends on actual rounded trace; Python snippet illustrative, no PyTorch backend equality. FP32.Arithmetic interface alone is uncertified, main theorem specifically instantiates FloatLib.

relevance: Useful full certificate closure and raw-weight table correspondence example for tiny transformers.
capability: Inspected FinalRaw theorem assembles raw-weight/table identities, exhaustive integer margins and analytic real-softmax bound to prove all12769 mod113 inputs. Also ACAS real-semantics tree checking, constructed fixed-weight networks and recurrent adder examples.
limitations: Integer weights at scale256 and exact-real softmax, explicitly not float checkpoint. Exhaustive tiny-model proof does not scale to GPTNeo. Generated proof modules live in release bundle; README discloses full source rebuild not established and ONNX importer audited/hash-pinned but unproved.
